correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the facewise length-distance potential: on a side face the straight apex ray has its own distance; on the base F(x)=min_j|x-Cν_j|, with C=a+sqrt(a²+h²). The virtual apex meets the actual base edge since |t*|<=a|tan θ|<=b, making the unfolded segment a valid attaining path; seam agreement and the intrinsic 1-Lipschitz bound prove equality, not merely a shortest-image heuristic. Strict inequality C²-(L²+b²)>=2a(L-a)>0 yields unique base-center maximum for h>0; radial quadratic root and uniform sector expansion give the ε²,ε³ coefficients, and direct inverse recovers all parameters. Separately integrated base-sector and lateral-face squared distances with 160-node Gauss–Legendre per variable for n=3,4,6,9 and two heights each (eight cases), agreeing with the exact second moment; independent small-ε root quadratures for n=3,4,7 converged to the cubic coefficient. These finite checks corroborate, do not prove, the all-parameter statement.
residual_risks: Zero height and nonregular/oblique pyramids excluded; no finite-sample stability follows from exact asymptotic inversion.
The cited virtual-source proof requires the basal surface included; using lateral surface only would change the theorem.
